Evaluate self-exciting (triggering) contributions at events and over the study domain

Source: R/trigger.R
trigger_evaluate.Rd

For every event \(i\), adds its triggering contribution \(g_T(t_j - t_i) \, g_S(x_j - x_i, y_j - y_i)\) to every other event \(j\) (this is 0 whenever \(t_j \le t_i\), because temporal_trigger and spatial_trigger vanish for non-positive/out-of-range offsets), and separately integrates its contribution over the full spatial grid and [0, TT]. The kernels are zero beyond the ends of their own grids, so that integral only evaluates them at the time marks and background-grid cells within their reach of the event; the rest would add exactly zero.

Usage

trigger_evaluate(
  events,
  background,
  temporal_trigger,
  spatial_trigger,
  exclude_self = TRUE,
  nprocs = 1
)

Arguments

events

A semihawkes_events object (from prepare_events()).

background

A semihawkes_spatial_base object (from background_spatial()) – only its grid and marks are used here, to define the spatial domain integrated over.

temporal_trigger

A semihawkes_trigger_temporal object (from trigger_temporal_init(), or a later Loop-k re-estimate).

spatial_trigger

A semihawkes_trigger_spatial object (from trigger_spatial_init(), or a later Loop-k re-estimate).

exclude_self

Whether to zero each event's contribution to itself; default TRUE.

nprocs

Parallel workers: a whole number (the default, 1, runs serially), "auto" to choose from the machine, or a cluster from parallel::makeCluster(), which is used and left running. "auto" uses one worker per physical core but one (two on a two-core machine), at most 2 while R CMD check runs, and runs serially for fewer than 1,000 events, where starting the workers costs more than they save. A number larger than the machine's cores is reduced to the number of cores, with a warning. The workers are socket clusters, which work on Windows, macOS and Linux, and the result is the same, to the last bit, whatever their number. Starting them takes up to a second, so for repeated calls pass a cluster; fit_semihawkes() does this itself.

Value

A list with at_events (numeric vector, one value per event: the total triggering contribution received from all other events) and at_all (single number: the same contribution integrated over the whole study region and [0, TT], summed across all events – i.e. mytriggers.at.events.no.A / mytriggers.at.all.no.A in the original script, without the A scaling parameter).

Examples

ev <- prepare_events(sim_events, sim_region, date_col = "date",
                     end_date = "2022-01-01")
#> The modelled study period ends on 2021-12-29, the day after the last event. `end_date` (2022-01-01) is used only to select events and to label outputs.
ev <- add_adaptive_bandwidth(ev, k = 5, min_dist = 150, min_bandwidth = 300)
ev <- add_bg_integral(ev, n_mc = 500, seed = 1)
bg <- background_spatial(ev, cell_size = 1000)
trig <- trigger_evaluate(ev, bg, trigger_temporal_init(),
                         trigger_spatial_init(x_range = 2000, x_step = 250))
summary(trig$at_events)
#>      Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max. 
#> 0.000e+00 2.035e-09 4.704e-09 6.385e-09 9.836e-09 2.511e-08 
trig$at_all
#> [1] 67.74254
